name: Confident Security
key_capability: Privacy and data-loss layer for AI interactions — wraps AI models to guarantee data privacy
notes: Came out of stealth with $4.2M seed funding

capability_assessment.rationale: CONFSEC is a confidential / provably-private AI inference layer (an enterprise build of Apple's Private Cloud Compute) — prompts and metadata stay unseen and unstored at inference via OHTTP, blind signatures, remote attestation, TEEs/TPMs, and transparency logs. All ten flags are false by design, and the design fact that makes them false is content-blindness: every flag in the set depends on detecting, classifying or enforcing on something, and CONFSEC is architecturally prevented from inspecting what passes through it. Nearest adjacency is llm_firewall, not dspm_ai_data_sec: as an OpenAI-compatible SDK and proxy, CONFSEC sits between the application and the model and so passes the placement test, but it runs no detectors of any kind and so fails the detector test. dspm_ai_data_sec is false because CONFSEC performs no detection or classification on prompt or upload content, not because DSPM is limited to data at rest — that premise was narrower than the definition, which covers data flowing into or out of AI, and than Ruling A, which reaches sensitive data in prompts, uploads and chats. ai_governance is false: its compliance surface (HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, GDPR and similar) contains no AI-specific framework, and the console governs spend and API keys rather than which AI tools or actions are allowed. Candidate trigger for an 11th dimension (confidential_inference) if more TEE-attestation inference vendors emerge. Originally assessed 2026-06-15; re-verified 2026-09-17 against docs/capability-definitions.md, which did not exist when the first assessment was written. The ten values hold; the 2026-06 reasoning did not, so verified_date moves to the re-verification.

The 2026-09-17 cloud-hosted browsing ruling does not settle this, because the browser is local; the open point is whether generic local controls applied to AI apps count as AI usage controls. Generic local controls (copy, paste, print, screen capture) applied to AI apps are not AI usage controls; definition 8 requires enforcement on AI use specifically, and Netskope's AI-specific endpoint client only discovers. All ten flags sourced.
